Ben — triage summary below (quick notes from log + automated signals):

- Observed pattern: 8 signups between 2026-10-10T22:40Z and 2026-10-11T03:05Z.
- Email domains: mixture of nomad.ai (3) and nomadai.io (5). Several addresses used +1 style variations (alice+dev@nomadai.io).
- IP signals: 6 distinct IPs, but all resolve to one ASN and share a narrow /24 block; reverse DNS shows dynamic hostnames (suspicious rotation).
- Device fingerprint: same browser UA and similar device fingerprints for 5 of the accounts.
- Heuristics tripped: rapid account creation (>=6 in 4h), device reuse, and prefix similarity. System set status to "provisional" and withheld auto-credits per Fraud Rule FR-17.

Recommended immediate actions:
1) Hold on manual reinstatement until CS verifies these are genuinely NomadAI employees (we can request corporate SSO or a specific header).
2) Run a quick check against our known partner whitelist; if NomadAI is a known partner, we can whitelist ASN for a short window.
3) Tag accounts as "under review" and set rollback window to 48 hours in case of false positive.

I've uploaded a snapshot of suspicious IPs to the SUP ticket and attached a PNG showing IP clustering.

Thanks Aditya — quick technical notes and a proposal for a low-friction customer experience:

Technical findings:
- Our FR-17 rule currently evaluates: account creation rate, email permutation score, device fingerprint reuse, and IP entropy. For this batch the combined score crossed the credit-block threshold.
- The rule doesn't distinguish SSO-backed corporate signups from self-serve emails.

Proposed changes (short term, low effort):
1) Per-IP credit issuance cap: soft cap of 3 credit-eligible signups per 24h per IP (log and alert after) — reduces burst abuse while preserving small dev teams.
2) Email policy tweak: if domain has existing verified company record in HubSpot (we have NomadAI), lower the weight of the permutation signal by 30% and defer to SSO verification.
3) Implement "grace review" workflow: when FR-17 triggers for a domain with >2 verified users in our DB, hold credits but auto-email a verification flow to the domain admin (template below). If admin confirms within 48h, auto-approve credits and record decision.

Customer impact estimate: may reduce false positives for legitimate startups by ~12% while catching >70% of rotating-bot bursts. We'll need a short notification template for CS so messaging is consistent.

Template (draft):
"Hi Priya — we flagged a set of signups from your domain for automated review because they matched high-rate creation signals. To complete verification we can accept a quick SSO assertion or a short confirmation from your security team. If you prefer, we can temporarily whitelist your ASN while we complete the check. Please reply with preferred contact. — Redwood Trust & Safety"

I can push the per-IP cap and the email-weight change as a config flip; implementing the full grace review UI will take an extra sprint. Marking SUP-2981 for the follow-up.

—Dev
